summary: OpenAI slashes prices by up to 80% on frontier models, following Google's lead amidst intensifying global competition.
details: The AI industry has entered a new phase where major players are drastically cutting costs and enhancing entry-level models to compete with emerging models from China.

caption:
AI token prices are plummeting as companies like OpenAI slash costs by up to 80%.

The AI industry has entered a new phase where major players are drastically cutting costs and enhancing entry-level models to compete with emerging models from China.

OpenAI recently reduced prices for its base ChatGPT 5.6 Luna model by 80% per million tokens and its 5.6 Terra model by 20%. This follows Google's introduction of more affordable Gemini Flash models.

Anthropic has replaced its most affordable Opus model with the more capable Claude 5.0 at the same price point, indicating a broader industry trend towards cost reduction.

This price war is driven by increased global competition, particularly from Chinese AI developers like DeepSeek and Moonshot, whose models offer comparable performance at lower costs.

The rapid price drops, such as OpenAI's GPT 5.6 Luna model becoming thirteen times cheaper than its GPT 5.4 predecessor within four months, highlight the intense pressure on AI companies.

These aggressive pricing strategies are occurring despite significant investments in compute power and ongoing concerns about AI's actual productivity gains in the workplace.

The financial implications are substantial, with OpenAI reportedly losing money on subscriptions and missing revenue targets, even as it commits to massive compute deals with partners like Oracle.
